GIF fixtures: how they were made
================================

Generated once, locally, on 2026-11-04 with Python 3 and Pillow 12.3.0. The
generator is a throwaway script and is NOT committed (the repository is 100%
Rust, ADR 032).

* still4_interlace0/1 (40x21, 4-colour palette), noise256_interlace0/1 (64x48
  seeded random indices on a 256-colour palette: forces 12-bit codes, a full
  LZW table and clear codes), gradient_interlaced (100x40), still2_bw (5x3,
  min code size 2), still_transparent_index1 (9x9 with the transparency
  index set; the palette entry for the transparent index is (0,0,0): our
  decoder leaves transparent pixels as (0,0,0,0), Pillow keeps the palette
  colour under alpha 0, so the fixture avoids comparing that unspecified RGB).
  Pillow only interlaces images at least 16 pixels in both directions, hence
  the sizes; tests assert the interlace flag really is set in the files.
* anim_disposal0..3: five 24x18 RGBA frames (transparent background, a few
  random opaque rectangles), saved with `disposal=n`, durations 40..200 ms,
  `loop=0`; Pillow crops frames to their changed rectangle.
* anim_loop3 (NETSCAPE loop value 3, so 4 plays), anim_noloop_ext (no NETSCAPE
  extension, 1 play), anim_opaque_local_palettes (three opaque 16x16 frames
  with different colours, so Pillow writes local colour tables).

Expected RGBA for every frame is Pillow's `seek(i).convert("RGBA")`, frames
concatenated, hashed with SHA-256. MANIFEST columns: name, width, height, frame
count, hash, plays (0 = forever; no loop extension = 1; extension value N
means N+1 plays), delays in ms.
